description: How a phone queues one saved edit (Android and iOS; the web has no queue). Given the versions this device knows, the queue (oldest first; `sent` once a command has been in a request) and the edit, the queue afterwards. If the entity's last queued command was never sent, the edit replaces it in place, keeping its command_id, base_version and position; but a delete that replaces a never-sent create (base_version 0) removes it instead, since the server never heard of the entity. Otherwise a new command is added at the end with base_version = the entity's last queued command's base_version + 1, or the known version (0 if unknown) when nothing is queued for it. Deleting a custom dhikr also drops never-sent commands for its dhikr_personal. The edit and its queue change are one local transaction; the queue's document for a delete is null (the wire command omits it). Phones only queue for a profile that belongs to an account (profile_switch).

sent.description: True once the command has been in a request, whether or not its receipt came back.

command_id.description: The new command's ID, if one is added.

sent.description: True once the command has been in a request, whether or not its receipt came back.

cases.description: With nothing queued for the entity, the command's base_version is the last version this device knows.
An entity the server has never seen has known version 0, so its first command creates it.
A command that was never sent is replaced in place: same command_id, base_version and queue position, new document.
Once a command has been sent it's never rewritten: the edit is a new command after it, on the version that command will produce (its base_version + 1).
After a sent create (base_version 0), the next command expects version 1.
Each sent command adds one: after sent commands on versions 3 and 4, the next expects 5.

cases.description: Deleting an entity whose create was never sent removes that create: the server never hears of the entity.
Deleting an entity whose create was already sent queues a delete on version 1.
A delete replaces an unsent update in place; the document goes.
Deleting a custom dhikr drops the unsent command for its dhikr_personal: the server deletes that record itself.
A dhikr_personal command already sent stays; only commands never sent are dropped.
A custom dhikr and its tags that never left the phone disappear from the queue entirely.

cases.description: Commands for other entities keep their place; the edit goes at the end.
Removing a dhikr's last tag is a put of an empty list; a dhikr_personal is never deleted by a client.
